bias_direction: I am biased toward this session looking productive, because it follows a session whose own attestation concedes 'thirty-three commits and zero rows of evidence' and I had an incentive to produce writes rather than another document. The concrete risk that creates: I repaired a bibliography and closed warrant fields, which are the cheapest DB writes available -- they touch five existing rows, admit no source, answer no research question, and move specifications not at all. A reviewer should read 15 updated fields as maintenance, not progress. Against that, a bias the other way: I authored the plan I then executed, so every act was one I had already argued for, and the one place that bias was tested -- the instruction to delete adjudication_integrity.py -- I only escaped by running the script instead of trusting my own text. Treat the acts I did NOT stop to re-measure as the weaker half of this session.
independent_reviewer_counterclaim: The strongest objection is that this session spent its effort on the layer it was warned about. The plan's own acceptance criterion is one answered question, published; specifications is still 0, search_executions is still 9, and no source was admitted -- so what landed is a corrected bibliography, corrected pointers in twenty-odd files, and corrections to three records about corrections. A reviewer is entitled to say that repairing the apparatus's account of itself is exactly the recursion the instrument was written to end, and that the fourth adversarial pass plus this execution have now produced more prose about the machine than the machine has produced about buildings. The honest answer is partly a concession: acts 0-3 are maintenance by construction, and the plan says so. The defence is narrower than it looks. Two of the fixes are load-bearing for the next act rather than decorative -- the retrieval-log extension bug would have turned a BLOCKING gate red on the first full-text fetch of act 2, and the scope finding means every tier in the corpus was underivable, which would have been inherited silently by the first determination. And the reason acts 4-6 did not run is not that they were skipped for cheaper work: they are gated on seven owner decisions, one of which (OD-A) determines whether any cell in this repository is determinable at all. A reviewer could still answer that discovering the deliverable is blocked on a decision nobody has been asked for is itself the finding, and that it should have been surfaced three sessions ago.
